checks.suggestion: Add a condition for credits available by mixed payment (part sight, part deferred) — confirm each portion matches its own draft.
checks.title: Where and how the credit is available
checks.body:
Read the availability terms together with the place of expiry. The key risk is when the credit is available with any bank, or when the availability method does not match the draft actually presented.

Fields to look at: {Available with}, {Place of presentation}, {Draft tenor}, {Place of expiry}

- If available with a named nominated bank: the place of expiry should sit with that bank.
- If available with any bank, no country specified: check the place of expiry against the country of presentation and flag routing risk.
- The availability method — sight, acceptance or negotiation — must match the draft presented.

checks.suggestion: No condition yet for transferring the insurance benefit to the second beneficiary — consider adding one.
checks.title: Transferable-credit routing
checks.body:
When the credit is transferable, watch where the second beneficiary sits and how documents are substituted. Routing a presentation through a third country can change the expiry and availability picture.

Fields to look at: {Available with}, {Beneficiary name}, {Place of expiry}

- If the second beneficiary is in a different country from the first: re-check the place of expiry and the presentation route.
- The substituted invoice and draft must still satisfy the original availability terms.

timeline.label: Proposed by assistant
timeline.detail: Suggested from a transferable-credit case. Awaiting confirmation.

checks.suggestion: You handle cross-border couriers but not electronic presentation (eUCP). Add a condition to skip the buffer when documents are presented electronically.
checks.title: Expiry buffer for presentation
checks.body:
Check whether the beneficiary has enough time to present documents before the LC expires. The key factor is whether the presentation location matches where the beneficiary is based — not simply whether it says "any bank."

Fields to look at: {Place of presentation}, {Expiry date}, {Beneficiary name}, {Latest shipment date}, {Presentation period}

- If the presentation location is in the beneficiary's own country: no extra buffer needed. {Expiry date} just needs to be later than the date documents would realistically be ready.
- If the presentation location is in a different country from the beneficiary (this can happen even with a nominated bank, not just "any bank"): add roughly 3-5 working days as a buffer, since documents need to be couriered cross-border.
- If it says "any bank" with no country specified: treat this the same as a local presentation — no buffer needed.

Note: the buffer is an operational risk flag, not a UCP requirement — don't treat it as a hard discrepancy, just something to warn about.

checks.title: Restricted-party screening
checks.body:
When any party, vessel or port on the documents appears on a sanctions or restricted-party list, hold the presentation and escalate before honouring.

Fields to look at: {Beneficiary name}, {Applicant name}, {Port of loading}, {Port of discharge}

- If any named party matches a restricted-party list: hold and escalate.
- If a vessel or port is subject to restrictions: hold and escalate.

checks.suggestion: Add an assertion for legalisation wording — three recent cases turned on it.
checks.title: Every document the credit calls for is present
checks.body:
Read {Documents required} as a list: one requirement per numbered or lettered item, and check the presentation against each in turn.

- A document of the type the item names is in the presentation.
- At least one original is presented, unless the item calls only for copies. "In triplicate" means one original and two copies.
- Where a full set is called for on a transport document, every original the document itself says was issued is presented.
- Signed, certified or legalised where the item says so.
- Issued by the party the item names, where it names one. If the issuer is worded differently but performs the same function, put it to a checker rather than raising it.
- The invoice is made out to the applicant, in the currency of the credit, and describes the goods as the credit does.
- No document is dated later than the date of presentation.

A sentence that qualifies every item ("all documents in English") applies to each document, not only the last one.

checks.suggestion: Split non-documentary conditions into their own assertion so they are reported as notes.
checks.title: Additional conditions are satisfied
checks.body:
Read {Additional conditions} one condition at a time — numbered items or sentences — and decide what, if anything, evidences each.

- A condition naming a document and something it must show: check that document carries the wording demanded.
- A condition fixing a value — credit number, incoterm, vessel, port — compare it with the field on the documents.
- A condition naming the issuer of a document: check the document was issued by that party.
- A condition setting timing: count from the shipment date, in calendar days unless it says banking days.
- A condition naming no document and no data point is non-documentary. Disregard it for the discrepancy list and report it to the checker as a note.

Where a condition repeats something the credit already requires elsewhere, raise it once, not twice.

refBook.desc: Availability, expiry date and place for presentation

UCP600 Art.6.summary: Where, how and until when the credit may be used.
UCP600 Art.6.read: A credit must name the bank with which it is available and the way it is available — sight payment, deferred payment, acceptance or negotiation. It must also state an expiry date and the place where documents are to be presented; presentation must be made on or before that date.

UCP600 Art.14.summary: The standard banks apply when examining documents.
UCP600 Art.14.read: Banks examine documents on their face to decide whether they form a complying presentation, taking up to five banking days. Data across documents need not be identical but must not conflict; addresses need only sit in the same country; a document may be dated before the credit but not after presentation.

UCP600 Art.18.summary: What a commercial invoice must show.
UCP600 Art.18.read: The invoice appears to be issued by the beneficiary, is made out to the applicant, is in the currency of the credit, and describes the goods in a way that corresponds to the credit. It need not be signed.

UCP600 Art.20.summary: Requirements for a bill of lading.
UCP600 Art.20.read: A bill of lading, however named, identifies the carrier and is signed correctly, shows the goods loaded on board a named vessel at the stated port of loading, and is the sole original or the full set issued.

UCP600 Art.28.summary: Insurance documents and the level of cover.
UCP600 Art.28.read: The insurance document is issued and signed by an insurer or agent, is dated no later than shipment unless it shows cover effective from shipment, is in the currency of the credit, and covers at least 110% of the CIF or CIP value.

UCP600 Art.29.summary: When the last day falls on a closed day.
UCP600 Art.29.read: If the expiry date or last day for presentation falls on a day the bank is closed for reasons other than force majeure, it extends to the first following banking day; the shipment-to-presentation period is not extended this way.

UCP600 Art.36.read: Banks assume no liability for business interrupted by acts of God, riots, wars or other causes beyond their control, and will not honour or negotiate under a credit that expired during such an interruption.

UCP600 Art.38.read: A credit can be transferred, in whole or part, to a second beneficiary only when it is expressly stated to be transferable. The transferred credit keeps the original terms except for permitted reductions in amount, unit price, expiry, presentation period and latest shipment.

ISBP821 A.read: Covers how to treat abbreviations, corrections, dates, spelling slips and the meaning of common terms, so examiners apply consistent judgement rather than mechanical matching.

ISBP821 E.read: Detailed guidance on dating, consignee and notify parties, on-board notations and clean documents when examining bills of lading and other transport documents.

bindings.note: 41A / 41D — the bank line before "BY"

fields.name: Available with

bindings.note: 41A / 41D — the text after "BY"

fields.name: Draft tenor
fields.description: The tenor the draft is drawn at.

bindings.note: Tag 42C, "drafts at"
The tenor phrase on the face: "at sight", "at 60 days after B/L date"

bindings.note: Tag 42A or 42D
Party named after "drawn on" or "to"

bindings.note: Tag 46A — whole block, kept unparsed for requirement cards

bindings.note: Tag 47A — whole block, kept unparsed for requirement cards

Goods lines under "description of goods" — ignore packing and freight notes
"Description of packages and goods" — may be in general terms

fields.description: Currency and amount of the credit, with any tolerance.

bindings.note: Tag 32B, widened by the 39A tolerance when present

Code beside the total
Currency of the sum insured

bindings.note: "Cover effective from" if shown, else the date of issue

fields.name: Latest shipment date

bindings.note: Tag 44C, or derived from the 44D shipment period

"Port of loading" or "from" — the named port, not a place of receipt

Shipper or consignor box

Party the invoice is made out to: "buyer", "consignee", "sold to", "bill to"
